verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 46.53
verses.english: Linked Discourses 46.53

verses.pali: 6. Sākacchavagga
verses.english: 6. Discussion

verses.pali: Aggisutta
verses.english: Fire

verses.pali: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṁ piṇḍāya pavisiṁsu.
verses.english: Then several mendicants robed up in the morning and, taking their bowls and robes, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

verses.pali: (Pariyāyasuttasadisaṁ.)
verses.english: (The same as the previous discourse.)

verses.pali: “Evaṁvādino, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā:
verses.english: “Mendicants, when wanderers of other religions say this, you should say to them:

verses.pali: ‘yasmiṁ, āvuso, samaye līnaṁ cittaṁ hoti, katamesaṁ tasmiṁ samaye bojjhaṅgānaṁ akālo bhāvanāya, katamesaṁ tasmiṁ samaye bojjhaṅgānaṁ kālo bhāvanāya?
verses.english: ‘Reverends, which awakening factors should not be developed when the mind is sluggish? And which awakening factors should be developed at that time?

verses.pali: Yasmiṁ panāvuso, samaye uddhataṁ cittaṁ hoti, katamesaṁ tasmiṁ samaye bojjhaṅgānaṁ akālo bhāvanāya, katamesaṁ tasmiṁ samaye bojjhaṅgānaṁ kālo bhāvanāyā’ti?
verses.english: Which awakening factors should not be developed when the mind is restless? And which awakening factors should be developed at that time?’

verses.pali: Evaṁ puṭṭhā, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā na ceva sampāyissanti, uttariñca vighātaṁ āpajjissanti.
verses.english: Questioned like this, the wanderers of other religions would be stumped, and, in addition, would get frustrated.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Yathā taṁ, bhikkhave, avisayasmiṁ.
verses.english: Because they’re out of their element.

verses.pali: Nāhaṁ taṁ, bhikkhave, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya yo imesaṁ pañhānaṁ veyyākaraṇena cittaṁ ārādheyya, aññatra tathāgatena vā tathāgatasāvakena vā ito vā pana sutvā.
verses.english: I don’t see anyone in this world—with its gods, Māras, and Divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—who could provide a satisfying answer to these questions except for the Realized One or his disciple or someone who has heard it from them.

verses.pali: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye līnaṁ cittaṁ hoti, akālo tasmiṁ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.
verses.english: When the mind is sluggish, it’s the wrong time to develop the awakening factors of tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Līnaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ taṁ etehi dhammehi dussamuṭṭhāpayaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Because it’s hard to stimulate a sluggish mind with these things.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso parittaṁ aggiṁ ujjāletukāmo assa.
verses.english: Suppose someone wanted to make a small fire flare up.

verses.pali: So tattha allāni ceva tiṇāni pakkhipeyya, allāni ca gomayāni pakkhipeyya, allāni ca kaṭṭhāni pakkhipeyya, udakavātañca dadeyya, paṁsukena ca okireyya;
verses.english: If they toss wet grass, cow-dung, and timber on it, spray it with water, and scatter dirt on it,

verses.pali: bhabbo nu kho so puriso parittaṁ aggiṁ ujjāletun”ti?
verses.english: could they make it flare up?”

verses.pali: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “No, sir.”

verses.pali: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ samaye līnaṁ cittaṁ hoti, akālo tasmiṁ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.
verses.english: “In the same way, when the mind is sluggish, it’s the wrong time to develop the awakening factors of tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Līnaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ taṁ etehi dhammehi dussamuṭṭhāpayaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Because it’s hard to stimulate a sluggish mind with these things.

verses.pali: Yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, samaye līnaṁ cittaṁ hoti, kālo tasmiṁ samaye dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.
verses.english: When the mind is sluggish, it’s the right time to develop the awakening factors of investigation of principles, energy, and rapture.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Līnaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ taṁ etehi dhammehi susamuṭṭhāpayaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Because it’s easy to stimulate a sluggish mind with these things.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso parittaṁ aggiṁ ujjāletukāmo assa.
verses.english: Suppose someone wanted to make a small fire flare up.

verses.pali: So tattha sukkhāni ceva tiṇāni pakkhipeyya, sukkhāni gomayāni pakkhipeyya, sukkhāni kaṭṭhāni pakkhipeyya, mukhavātañca dadeyya, na ca paṁsukena okireyya;
verses.english: If they toss dry grass, cow-dung, and timber on it, blow on it, and don’t scatter dirt on it,

verses.pali: bhabbo nu kho so puriso parittaṁ aggiṁ ujjāletun”ti?
verses.english: could they make it flare up?”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “Yes, sir.”

verses.english: “In the same way, when the mind is sluggish, it’s the right time to develop the awakening factors of investigation of principles, energy, and rapture.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Līnaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ taṁ etehi dhammehi susamuṭṭhāpayaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Because it’s easy to stimulate a sluggish mind with these things.

verses.pali: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye uddhataṁ cittaṁ hoti, akālo tasmiṁ samaye dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.
verses.english: When the mind is restless, it’s the wrong time to develop the awakening factors of investigation of principles, energy, and rapture.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Uddhataṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ taṁ etehi dhammehi duvūpasamayaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Because it’s hard to settle a restless mind with these things.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso mahantaṁ aggikkhandhaṁ nibbāpetukāmo assa.
verses.english: Suppose someone wanted to extinguish a great mass of fire.

verses.pali: So tattha sukkhāni ceva tiṇāni pakkhipeyya, sukkhāni ca gomayāni pakkhipeyya, sukkhāni ca kaṭṭhāni pakkhipeyya, mukhavātañca dadeyya, na ca paṁsukena okireyya;
verses.english: If they toss dry grass, cow-dung, and timber on it, blow on it, and don’t scatter dirt on it,

verses.pali: bhabbo nu kho so puriso mahantaṁ aggikkhandhaṁ nibbāpetun”ti?
verses.english: could they extinguish it?”

verses.pali: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “No, sir.”

verses.pali: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ samaye uddhataṁ cittaṁ hoti, akālo tasmiṁ samaye dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.
verses.english: “In the same way, when the mind is restless, it’s the wrong time to develop the awakening factors of investigation of principles, energy, and rapture.

verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Uddhataṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ taṁ etehi dhammehi duvūpasamayaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Because it’s hard to settle a restless mind with these things.

verses.english: When the mind is restless, it’s the right time to develop the awakening factors of tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

verses.english: Why is that?

verses.english: could they extinguish it?”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “Yes, sir.”

verses.pali: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ samaye uddhataṁ cittaṁ hoti, kālo tasmiṁ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya.
verses.english: “In the same way, when the mind is restless, it’s the right time to develop the awakening factors of tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Uddhataṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ taṁ etehi dhammehi suvūpasamayaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Because it’s easy to settle a restless mind with these things.

verses.pali: Satiñca khvāhaṁ, bhikkhave, sabbatthikaṁ vadāmī”ti.
verses.english: But mindfulness is always useful, I say.”

verses.pali: Tatiyaṁ.
